verdicts.reason: The user at CLIENT01 starts the connection. The rdp01.1sn0s.lab label is visible. The caption 'Secure RDP connection' is correct. Nothing shows the client owning a certificate.
An amber pulse runs along the floor channel from the client to rdp01. Pending colour, network channel only.
The listener lights on the server face. The caption 'The RDP server needs a trusted identity' is on screen. The server owns the identity.

A pale card labelled 'Self-signed' (signed by itself, not unsigned) travels to the client and is tagged 'Unverified'. The channel stays amber, then the amber dies out (strip frame 6: the channel is grey), so the attempt ends.
The RDPAuth badge comes from the 1SN0S.LAB AD node and settles on rdp01. No client connection is pending, and no key or certificate comes from AD.
The key pair forms inside the opened chassis: a private key with a padlock motif and a ring-headed public key. The caption 'The private key stays on the server' is on screen.
The private key drops into the lidded key container (strip frame 2), the lid closes and it locks. The public key stays outside.
The public key enters the white capsule while the container stays closed. The caption 'The request is signed, not the key sent' is on screen.
A light beam from the closed container seals the capsule with a band. Nothing key-shaped travels.

The capsule waits outside the server at its port, framed with the 1SN0S.LAB pillar. A steel-blue diamond query goes to AD, and a cyan floor route lights to Issuing CA 1 only. In B-04.1_b the capsule sits visually near the AD pillar's foot, but later frames place it at the server, and it never enters AD.
The capsule travels along the lit cyan route into the Issuing CA 1 vault. It does not go near the root.

Only three of the four F-06 checks can be read. 'Requester authenticated' sits behind the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' label in every frame, and the capsule covers part of 'Enroll permission granted'. As shown, authentication of the requester is never stated.

The capsule is consumed and a card stamped 'rdp01.1sn0s.lab / Remote Desktop Authentication' comes out (EKU correct). However, from about f1009 a white open-ring shape with a stub appears at the press head (strip frame 2; B-04.4_b near x475,y170; B-04.4_c near x440,y185) and stays there afterwards. It is not present before signing (B-04.3 frames) and has no counterpart on Issuing CA 2's press. Its silhouette reads as key-like material outside the sealed module, and nothing shows the CA key still inside the module.

The card travels back and locks beside the closed key container, and the key does not move. Issuing CA 1's crown card stays in place. The intermediate copy is hard to separate visually here, but it is present at presentation (B-06.1).

A gold vault on a plinth with no cables, labelled '1SN0S Root CA', with a static ring seal and a dark press. A small dark cube appears on the plinth during the beat (strip frames 4-6, absent at f1193); see the minor finding.

The desaturated flashback is marked 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony'. The capsule tagged 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' is carried to the root, and the caption is correct. However, the 'earlier' Issuing CA 1 vault still shows the RDP enrollment check list ('Template published on this CA', 'Enroll permission granted', 'Request meets template policy') and the stamped-press state from B-04.3/B-04.4 (T-cut f1246, B-05.2_a, B-05.2_c). This presents a CA that has not yet been certified as having already approved the RDP request, and it ties the RDP enrollment to the root ceremony.

A trust link grows from the root seal to Issuing CA 1's crown certificate, and the root stays cable-free. The caption 'The Root CA is the trust anchor' is used for the root only. The link renders near-white rather than gold-to-cyan (minor).

A fresh amber pulse runs from the client to the server, then two cyan cards (the server certificate and its own intermediate copy) travel to the client. No key shape travels. The key pulse and the impression are too small to read at this scale, but nothing contradicts F-10.
The cards dock upward under a gold root already in its cradle, tagged 'Installed earlier by policy'. Nothing travels from AD.
'Missing intermediate? AIA can fetch it' and 'Fetching never creates trust' appear, and nothing is fetched.
Six distinct checks appear: chain, signatures, validity, name rdp01.1sn0s.lab, EKU, and revocation pending in amber.
Two amber CRL fetches come from pki.1sn0s.lab and dock on the server certificate and the intermediate only. The gold root gets none. 'OCSP if deployed' sits on the client's list.
The channel turns from amber to green after all ticks pass, and the session window opens. The caption fades in slightly before the green (minor).
The camera glides to WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab with its WebServer-TLS badge.
A local key pair forms, the private key is locked in the container, and a beam from the container seals the capsule. No key travels.

A steel-blue query goes to AD. Issuing CA 1 is tagged 'WebServer-TLS not published here', and Issuing CA 2 carries the four eligibility tags with a violet route. The capsule waits at WEB01. Issuing CA 1 stays cyan instead of muted grey (minor).
The capsule travels only along the violet route into Issuing CA 2.

'Requester authenticated' is hidden behind the '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' label again. The note 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is printed on top of 'Request meets template policy', so neither can be read. The F-06/F-07 content the beat exists to carry is lost.
The capsule is consumed at the press, and a 'portal.1sn0s.lab / Server Authentication' card travels back to WEB01 beside its container. The EKU is correct.
The existing crown certificate of Issuing CA 2 is linked to the same root seal. The root press stays dark and there are no cables.

The amber channel goes to the web server, two violet cards dock under the gold root, and the ticks read name portal.1sn0s.lab, EKU TLS server auth, validity and revocation. The channel then turns green.

The root is on top, with the two CAs and their servers below. Cyan and violet paths rise to the single root, the root stays cable-free, and the caption is correct. The convergence renders white rather than gold (minor).
The title card 'Certificate Flow — From request to trust' appears, followed by a fade to black and a clean end.

findings.evidence: From about f1009 a white open-ring shape with a stub appears at Issuing CA 1's press head (B-04.4_b near x475,y170; B-04.4_c near x440,y185) and stays there through B-04.5 and into the flashback. It is not present before signing (B-04.3_c) and is not present on Issuing CA 2's press (B-08.2). The sealed module never visibly holds the key.
findings.why: A key-like silhouette outside the sealed module, at the press, reads as Issuing CA 1's private key having left its protected storage to sign. If it is key material, this is a BLOCKER-class F-03 violation. At best it is ambiguous.
findings.direction: Keep every element at the press head clearly non-key (no ring-and-stub silhouette). Show the signing as light or drive from the closed module only, and make the module visibly sealed with its key inside.

findings.evidence: Check 1, 'Requester authenticated', sits behind the '1SN0S Issuing CA 1' label in every frame. The capsule covers the middle of 'Enroll permission granted'.
findings.why: F-06 requires all four checks to be shown, and requester authentication is the first. The viewer sees only publication, permission and policy, so 'arriving is never sufficient' is weakened.
findings.direction: Keep all four check lines unoccluded and readable throughout the beat (move the CA label or the list, and keep the capsule clear of the text).

findings.evidence: 'Requester authenticated' is hidden behind the '1SN0S Issuing CA 2' label. The note 'Name supplied in request — enrollment restricted' is drawn over 'Request meets template policy', and both are illegible.
findings.why: The beat exists to show the same four checks plus the F-07 restriction for a subject-supplied template. Neither the authentication check nor the restriction note can be read.
findings.direction: Give the note its own line clear of the check list, and keep check 1 visible.

findings.evidence: Inside the 'Earlier' flashback, Issuing CA 1's vault still shows the RDP enrollment check list ('Template published on this CA', 'Enroll permission granted', 'Request meets template policy') with ticks, and the post-signing press state from B-04.3/B-04.4.
findings.why: At setup Issuing CA 1 has no CA certificate and has issued nothing. Showing the RDP request's completed checks during the root ceremony links the RDP enrollment to the root signing, which the spec's flashback constraint explicitly guards against.
findings.direction: In the flashback era, show Issuing CA 1 in its pre-certification state with no RDP check list, press output or RDP-era residue.

findings.evidence: A dark cube materialises on the root plinth beside the press during B-05.1 (absent at f1193, present from strip frame 4) and stays for the rest of the film.
findings.why: Something appearing on the root in the present tense can read as root activity or output. The root must perform no operation in the present.
findings.direction: Have the plinth's fixtures present from the root's first appearance, or remove the object.

findings.evidence: Issuing CA 1 keeps its cyan colour while tagged 'WebServer-TLS not published here'. It does not dim to muted grey.
findings.why: The ineligible CA should read as ineligible by colour as well as by text (spec B-07.3, C-10).
findings.direction: Dim Issuing CA 1 to the ineligible grey token for the eligibility lookup.

findings.evidence: An amber pulse dot stays at the server end of the RDP channel after it has turned green, and later at the web channel's end.
findings.why: Amber means pending. A pending marker on a validated connection contradicts the established-trust state.
findings.direction: Retire the amber pulse when the channel turns green.

findings.evidence: The issuer links from the CA crowns to the root seal render near-white instead of gold-to-cyan and gold-to-violet converging in gold.
findings.why: The gold convergence is what visually ties both paths to the single trust anchor.
findings.direction: Use the role colours on the trust links, with gold at the root end.

findings.evidence: The caption 'Trusted RDP connection established' is visible while the channel is still amber.
findings.why: The caption claims trust before the channel shows it.
findings.direction: Bring the caption in only once the channel has turned green.
